verdict: Equifax grew revenue 10% to $1.7B — US information services up 13% and US mortgage revenue up 15% despite a weak housing market — and profit rose 32% to $212M as admin costs fell from last year's level.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $1,693M, vs $1,545M a year ago; 9% in local currency

kpis.label: Workforce Solutions
kpis.note: Up 7% — employment and income verification, the biggest segment

kpis.label: U.S. mortgage revenue
kpis.note: Growth despite a weaker mortgage market — USIS mortgage revenue alone was up 28%

segments.name: Workforce Solutions
segments.note: Checking people's employment and income for employers and lenders — Verification Services brought in $603M (up 9%) and Employer Services $91M (down 5%).

segments.name: U.S. Information Solutions
segments.note: Credit data and scores for US lenders — Online Information Solutions $530M (up 13%) plus Financial Marketing Services $69M (up 11%). Mortgage revenue was the standout, up 28% inside this segment.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Credit bureaus outside the US — Latin America $114M, Asia Pacific $108M, Europe $106M and Canada $72M.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the data products and running the company — down 10% YoY, the main reason profit jumped.

otherDetail: Other was -$58.5M, net: $3.8M of other income minus $62.3M of interest expense.
oneTimers: Acquisition-related costs of $9M ($6M after tax) were booked in operating costs in the quarter, tied to integrating recent deals — small, but they are the kind of cost Equifax strips out of its adjusted figures.
footerNote: Equifax gives no gross-profit line. Cost of revenue here combines its cost of services ($752M) with depreciation and amortization ($194M) — the full cost of delivering its data services — leaving selling, general and administrative costs as the operating-expense line; the split follows the release's own expense order. Net income in the flow is consolidated net income of $213M; the profit attributable to Equifax, which the release headlines, was $212M after $2M attributable to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: Rows are rounded to the nearest cent per $100; the chain adds to $12.60 of profit per $100 versus the $12.61 shown, a 1-cent rounding difference. Kept-as-profit is consolidated net income; $12.51 of it is attributable to Equifax.

takeaways.title: Growth was broad-based
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 10% to $1,693M. Workforce Solutions grew 7% to $694M, US Information Solutions 13% to $599M and International 9% to $400M. Products outside plain credit reports — what Equifax calls Diversified Markets — grew 8% and now cushion the mortgage cycle.

takeaways.title: Mortgage beat a weak market
takeaways.text: US mortgage revenue rose 15% even as the housing market weakened late in the quarter, and USIS mortgage revenue rose 28%. New products built on the EFX Cloud and its AI tools set a record vitality index above 17% — the share of revenue from recently launched products.

takeaways.title: Costs fell, profit jumped
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Equifax rose 32% to $212M and diluted EPS to $1.79 from $1.29. The swing factor was selling, general and administrative costs falling 10% to $390M, which more than offset a 13% rise in the cost of delivering services. Equifax also returned $158M to shareholders in buybacks and dividends.
